title: Paths in a dependent pair type: the path type is equivalent to the dependent sum of a base path and a path over it

standard_prerequisites: Dependent pair types (Sigma types) with their induction principle (pair induction).
Transport along a path in a type family, with its definitional behaviour on reflexivity.
Dependent paths over a base path: paths in the total space project to base paths with a lifting condition.
The induction principle for identity types (path induction) and equivalences via quasi-inverse.
core_obligations: Construct, by path induction, the canonical function from w = w' in the total space to the dependent sum over base paths p of the type of identifications of the transported second component with the target second component.
Construct the reverse function by pair induction, Sigma induction, and path induction, reducing everything to reflexivity.
Prove both composite identifications by staged inductions breaking apart the pairs and the paths.
Conclude that the canonical function is an equivalence, so paths in a Sigma type are exactly pairs of a base path and a path over it.
proof_roadmap: Define the forward map f by path induction: on reflexivity w = w it outputs the pair of reflexivity of the first projection and reflexivity of the second projection.

Define the reverse map g: induct on w and w-prime to split them into pairs; apply Sigma induction to the input to obtain a base path p and an over-path q; induct on p to reduce transport along reflexivity to the identity, and induct on q to reduce the goal to reflexivity of the pair.

Verify f of g of r equals r: break apart w, w-prime, and r by pair induction, reduce both components of r to reflexivity by path induction, and check the composite is definitionally the identity on the pair of reflexivity paths.
Verify g of f of p equals p: path induction on p, then pair induction on w, reduces both sides to reflexivity of the pair, again by definition.
Conclude that f is a quasi-inverse equivalence, giving the announced equivalence for all w, w-prime.
difficulty_reason: A four-stage induction argument (path induction, pair induction, Sigma induction, and component path inductions in a careful order) proving both quasi-inverse directions for the Sigma-type path characterization.
